main_text.p: folymae ablata,ac in regales ulus ufurpata, sed recondita in thelauris habebantur, proferri imperavit. Cum his per luxu ac licentiam regalis convivii promiscue omnes{a}o-mnis virilis ac muliebris sexus,uxores concubinaeq; ejus uterentur,subito rex in pa-riete conspicit digitos scribentes: cerne-[?]bantur; {b}inversum ductae literae. Sed qui posseт scripta legere,non reperiebatur. Igitur rex perterritus, magos & Chaldaeos advocat. Quibus mussitantibus,nec quic-quā respondentibus,{c}regina regę admo-net, esse quendā Hebraeum Daniel nomine, qui olim Nabuchodonosor occulti mysterii somnium revelasset,jam tum ob illustrem sapientiam summis honoribus donatum. Itaq; accitus Daniel,perlegit interpretatusq; ob delictum regis, qui sacra Deo vasa temerasset, ipsi exitium immi-nere, regnumque ejus Medis ac Persis da-tum: quod mox consecutum est. nam eadem nocte Balthasar interiit,regnumque ejus Darius natione Medus occupavit: qui Danielem illustri opinione compertum, universo impetio praepoluit, secundus superiorum regum judicium. Nam & Nabuchodonosor cum regno praefe-cerat,

page.notes: Left margin notes, read top to bottom, are partly blurred: "omnes" (ref. a), "Sig.", "Balthasar", "rex sacris" [?], "vasis abu- tentis ul- rio." [?], "in candelabrum" (ref. b, printed "in can- delabrum"), "versum.", "Idem." and "Aria," (ref. c) [?], "Iosephus", "Dan. 4.", "Darius rex.", "Dan. 5.", "Ier. 50." Several note words are cut off at the edge and the reading is uncertain. In the text: "cerne-bantur" is hard to read at the line end; "mussitantibus" and "impetio" are uncertain readings; "posseт" contains a stray Cyrillic-looking letter in my draft and should read "posset" [?]. The text runs on to the next page after "praefe-cerat,".
